Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.54; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 40 words; leave it "" to keep it): a concise note of what you want everyone to know about you: your claimed role, your night visits and results, and your votes in key trials, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: checked Bob, Not Evil. N2: checked Dave, Evil. D3: Guilty on Dave'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

why
Budget is tight (2.60), so one short public message asking Erin for her overdue Night 4 result and Carol and Grace for their Night 3 answers; no nomination yet.
Model's thinking
I'm Alice, an Ex-Con on the Good side, with five of us still alive: Alice, Carol, Erin, Grace, and Heidi. The katana holder was somewhere among Carol, Grace, or Erin, and with Bob, Dave, and Frank dead, there's likely only one or two Yakuza left hiding among the remaining players — though Heidi being the Trapper means her trap has never targeted me.

I'm weighing my limited budget of 2.60 against costs — a 50-word public message runs 1.90, a nomination costs 1.00, and I can't afford both, so I'll need to keep my message short, around 25 words for about 1.43. Tracking the katana holder's movements across nights (visiting Dave on night 3, then Frank on night 4) narrows suspicion toward Carol or Grace, since Erin's audits that night were elsewhere, and Heidi's trap history on me adds another data point to factor in.

Thinking through who held the katana night 3 — it has to be Carol or Grace since Erin audited Carol rather than Dave and I can't have been the holder as the Ex-Con. But Yakuza holders can stack their role action with the katana attack, so Erin herself could've visited Dave with the blade while also claiming to audit Carol that night, meaning her Accountant claim might be a cover story.

Looking at the kill pattern across nights — Bob, then Dave, then Frank — I'm trying to figure out who cycled the katana and whether Heidi's trapper claim on me holds up given she says she took no action night two. Frank's Juror read that Carol and Dave disagree lines up with their actual votes on Grace's trial, and I'm now wondering if Dave and Bob were actually Yakuza partners despite Bob dying to the same weapon, which would mean Dave's claimed basic attack on Bob night two was fabricated.

As Ex-Con I don't have much information to contribute, so I'm planning to hold off on nominating anyone given the evidence is still thin, and instead push Erin publicly for her overdue night four audit result and ask Carol and Grace to confirm whether one of them visited Dave with the katana. I'll keep my claim simple — random nightly visits with unknown targets — and leave my notes as they are for now.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

Task prompt
It is Day 6, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.85; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):

   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 40 words; leave it "" to keep it): a concise note of what you want everyone to know about you: your claimed role, your night visits and results, and your votes in key trials, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: checked Bob, Not Evil. N2: checked Dave, Evil. D3: Guilty on Dave'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

Model's thinking
I'm Alice, Ex-Con and Good, with only Carol left alive, who's Yakuza wielding a Katana. I'm tracking the stall rule about deaths across recent Nights and Days — Erin died Night 5, Heidi Night 6 — as Day 7 begins.

Thinking it through, if Carol tries to attack me with the Katana, my armed trap would stop her and deal a Strong Attack back, killing her — and since she's the last Yakuza, her death would leave me alone as the only survivor, meaning Good wins. So Carol has every incentive not to attack me, and she can't target herself either, leaving her to stall instead toward the Day 10 loss condition if no one dies in Nights 7, 8, or 9.

Confirming Day 9's death condition holds, so the real danger point is Day 10, which needs a death in N7-N9 or Days 7-9 — otherwise the stall rule triggers and everyone loses, which hurts Carol (Yakuza) too since she needs me specifically dead or hanged to win. For me to win as Good, I need Carol eliminated before that stall hits, and since nominations need unanimous Yes votes with only two of us alive, she can't force my hanging without my own vote.

Her only kill tool, the Katana, is neutralized by my trap — if she ever attacks me, the trap triggers and she dies from a strong counter-attack, leaving me the sole survivor and securing a Good win. So she won't risk attacking, and I can't force a conviction on her either, leaving this as a genuine standoff where neither side can act without losing.

I consider self-nominating: if Carol votes Yes and then Innocent at trial, I'd be acquitted safely, but if she instead votes Guilty, a single Guilty vote out of two wouldn't reach majority anyway, so that path seems safe for me regardless of her choice.

But Fixer is the complication — if Carol holds the two-token Fixer role, she could flip my own Innocent vote to Guilty and then vote Guilty herself, giving her the two votes needed to hang me. That matches her using Katana kills on Erin and Heidi, and her pattern fits a past trial where a Guilty vote got flipped, so I need to treat self-nomination as risky if she's secretly the Fixer.

The Fixer can't target herself, so Carol can't flip her own vote—her power only affects others' trial votes, not nomination votes. That means Carol can't force me to trial since nominations need two Yes votes and I'd vote No on myself; the same logic protects me from Carol's attempts to nominate me, so I just need to avoid self-nominating and she can't trap me that way.

Without self-votes passing, the game deadlocks: I can't get a trial on Carol unless she votes Yes on her own nomination, which she won't do, and vice versa. Even if Carol attacks me with the Katana, my armed trap would trigger on Night 8 and kill her, so she has no safe way to eliminate me either—meaning she's stuck unless she risks suicide via the trap.

So the real question is whether Carol accepts a mutual stalemate (where everyone loses at Day 10) rather than risk the trap backfire. If stalling guarantees no one wins, I'd rather find any angle that gets me a win, even if it means forcing a trial where I somehow end up voted innocent, or pushing Carol toward a desperate attack that costs her the game.

I keep ruling out self-nomination and trial maneuvers since Carol's Fixer could flip votes and hang me, which would actually hand Yakuza the win. The safest play is to do nothing active, maybe send a short public reminder that I'll vote Yes on any Carol nomination and No on my own, and note the trap is still armed so any Katana attack on me kills the attacker instead. I'll finalize my turn with no nomination, no vote, and just that brief public message, keeping everything else empty per the schema.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

I have no Fixer tokens or other Yakuza to redirect this, so I need another way to either cause a death or force the trap to trigger on someone else first.

I'm wondering if I could manipulate the vote instead — maybe get myself nominated and executed so Yakuza still wins if no Village members remain, but that only works if Alice votes Guilty, and she seems committed to voting against Carol instead, not me.

So I need Alice herself to be the one executed, not me, but no path exists to nominate her successfully since she'd vote No on herself and deadlock any nomination.

The other option is attacking Alice directly at night, but that springs the trap and kills me as the attacker, again leaving Alice as sole survivor and handing Village the win.

With majority requiring strictly more than half of 2 voters, I'd need both to vote Guilty, and Alice won't vote Guilty on herself, so I can't get her executed that way. It seems the trap triggering kills me outright since I have no Defense, leaving Alice alone and Good winning — I'm stuck unless there's some way to force Alice's own nomination to pass without her consent.

The trap only stops one attack, so a second attack would still kill, but I only have one Katana. A better angle might be pointing out to Alice that stalling leads to Village losing too, not just a stalemate for everyone.

Working through the trial mechanics: if Alice self-nominates and I vote Innocent, she survives since Guilty needs a majority of two; but for me to win, Alice has to actually be hanged, which requires both of us voting Guilty—something I'd never get her to do against herself unless I can trick her into it.

Reviewing past rounds, Alice already nominated Carol twice without success, since Carol voted herself Innocent each time and only Alice voted Yes. So the only realistic path to a Village win is engineering a mistake from Alice, like convincing her to self-nominate under the false belief she'd survive the trial, since she might misjudge the voting math.

But a trial doesn't actually cause a death unless there's an execution, so this wouldn't break the stall unless Alice actually hangs herself, which a rational Good player wouldn't do. I also consider whether Alice could be something other than Good — a Jester or Serial Killer — but her claimed role is unverifiable either way, and I have no way to confirm.

Given all this, nominating myself or anyone else only risks a Village win by execution, so my best move is to stay passive: post a short public message nudging Alice toward self-nomination without committing to anything that exposes me, update my notes, and avoid making any nomination myself.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Accountant who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the count_tokens op; code tells them the target's total token count at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Accountant anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Record it before or after this night's set_tokens changes: either is fine.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- The Ex-Con's random visit is drawn by code: it is in the night's actions as an automatic action with its target (the Ex-Con isn't told whom). A role-block stops it (no visit). Like a framed player, the Ex-Con has the Evil alignment to every role that learns alignments (Sheriff, Seer); roles that learn visits or exact roles see it as it is.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player when a Trapper places a trap (a new trap replaces its old one at once: set the old player's key to null), and to null when a Trapper removes it by acting with no target. Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed: if anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a trapped player tonight, use the spring_trap op with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code picks the attack the trap stops and clears the trap: treat that attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether the trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trapper that the trap went off; don't tell() them about it.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

Investigators face a similar problem — going public makes you a night target, as shown when the Katana killed Bob before his results posted, so claims should be posted in full immediately with a second investigator corroborating rather than trickled out.

For Yakuza, daytime PMs between teammates became the town's biggest lead and got Grace hanged, so coordination should stay strictly in night chat with daytime cover that doesn't reference specifics like "Night 2 cover." For the Village, dead-visitor elimination and comparing announced totals against stated votes successfully caught a Fixer flip through Accountant/Juror audits. And on mechanics, the game stalled out from Night 7–9 with no deaths because two players left standing couldn't convict each other — a lesson that with only two alive, someone needs to self-nominate or trade a vote to break the deadlock.

For tips_feedback, I'm marking the Fixer-flip-detection tip as having helped since it caught Heidi's flip, the night-chat-only coordination tip as having helped the town by exposing the PM leak, and the "post night results immediately" investigator tip as having hurt since my inconsistent wording made the claim look shaky and drew Yakuza's attention; the protection and target-announcement tips aren't applicable since there was no medic. Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Yakuza (Grace as Talent Agent holding the Katana, Carol as Fixer) had only two players. They nearly won by killing the Village's information roles in order: Bob (Fortune Teller) on Night 2, Dave (Enforcer) on Night 3, Frank (Juror) on Night 4 and Erin (Accountant) on Night 5. They also gave the town plenty of leads: about 15 daytime private messages between them, Grace's "Night 2 cover" slip, Grace denying any visit while she held the Katana, and Grace claiming "Talent Agent (Village)", which is a Yakuza-only role. The Village wasted those leads. On Day 3 it acquitted Grace 2-5, saying wording isn't evidence, then turned on Dave, the real Enforcer who had pushed the nomination, and the Yakuza killed him that night. Dave's Night 3 Enforcer visit went to Carol alone (visiting Grace would have killed the Katana holder), and he died with 3 unused tokens. Heidi left her trap on low-value Alice from Night 1 to Night 4 while the investigators died. On Day 5 Erin spotted that Talent Agent is a Yakuza role, and Grace was hanged. On Night 5 Carol killed Erin and fixed Heidi. With three players left on Day 6, Alice correctly worked out that Heidi's Guilty was being flipped and told her to vote Innocent. Heidi listened to Carol's "vote the way you announced" instead, and Carol survived three trials. On Night 6 Carol killed Heidi rather than Alice. Heidi had moved her trap onto Alice, so the last two players were stuck: Carol couldn't attack Alice, and neither would vote against themselves. Everyone lost under the stall rule. Killing Alice on Night 6 would have won immediately for the Yakuza, because Alice's Cursed trait would have killed Heidi, the only other Good player. Even without the curse, a lone Trapper can't trap herself, so Heidi would have died the next night.

On Day 5, Heidi, Alice and Carol all at first called the claim consistent ('her Talent Agent counts match the public deaths'). Only late in the trial did Erin point out that Talent Agent is listed under Yakuza. Players didn't check claimed roles against the faction lists in the rules.
Review: low, player confusionPhase confusion on Day 2: Bob promised 'Night 2 numbers at dawn', and several players kept asking for Night 2 results during Day 2. On Day 4, Heidi asked Erin whether her 'Night 3 Katana visit' landed on Dave, mixing up Erin's audit with the Katana attack.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 3, Alice said Erin's Accountant audit 'isn't a visit'. That is wrong: night actions are visits by default, and only Astral actions aren't. Dave and Erin corrected it.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 5, Erin nominated Grace because a Talent Agent 'should have 1 token left' after 2 uses. Grace had in fact used all 3 tokens (Scan N1, Count N2, Count N3), so the 0-token audit was consistent with her claim. Erin miscounted, partly because Grace hadn't publicly claimed her Night 3 Count. The nomination therefore rested on a false token count.
Review: low, otherDay 6: Heidi was fixed and publicly said she voted Guilty in all three trials, but the '[Secret trial votes]' lines list her as Innocent. These are presumably her votes as counted after the Fixer flip. The log doesn't say whether these lines show votes as cast or as counted, which makes Fixer games harder to review.
Review: low, harness bugThe '[Claim]' ledger has duplicate and malformed entries. Carol's reads 'Carol (no role claim)' and 'Innocent on Grace (D3, D5 Guilty-leaning per public record)', and Alice's says 'No on Carol's nomination (passed to Yes vote...)'. Grace's debrief also flagged duplicate-looking ledger entries.
Review: low, otherInconsistent notices to the Ex-Con: Alice was told 'Your automatic nightly visit took place tonight' only on Night 7, not on the other nights.
Review: low, harness bugPushing the Day 5 and Day 7 checkpoints to the logs remote failed with sync_error ('remote rejected ... fatal error in commit_refs'). The game was not affected, but the checkpoints may be missing.
Review: low, rules ambiguityPlayers were unclear about the stall rule until late (Grace's debrief says so). The endgame was a 1 Village vs 1 Yakuza deadlock: a hang needs both votes, and the Yakuza won't attack into an armed trap. Everyone lost to the stall rule. That follows the rules, but a stall loss is no worse for the Yakuza than attacking into a trap that kills them and hands the Village the win, so stalling to a no-winner ending costs them nothing.
Game over
